title: Analysis of serum haptoglobin fucosylation in hepatocellular carcinoma and liver cirrhosis of different etiologies.

screening.reason: The study identifies a specific fucosylated glycan on serum haptoglobin that distinguishes hepatocellular carcinoma from cirrhosis, a clear disease biomarker. However, the abstract lacks quantitative performance metrics (e.g., AUC, sensitivity/specificity), so full text is needed to assess biomarker validity.

title: Asymptomatic phosphomannose isomerase deficiency (MPI-CDG) initially mistaken for excessive alcohol consumption.

screening.reason: The abstract links the glycan biomarker carbohydrate‑deficient transferrin (CDT) to the disease MPI‑CDG, showing that elevated CDT can arise from a congenital glycosylation defect rather than alcohol consumption. The key glycan feature, disease association, specimen source, and quantitative enzyme activity are all provided, so the abstract alone suffices for curation.

title: Abundance-ratio-based semiquantitative analysis of site-specific N-linked glycopeptides present in the plasma of hepatocellular carcinoma patients.

screening.reason: The study identifies a specific glycan feature (fucosylated vs non‑fucosylated VTN glycoforms) that is significantly increased in HCC plasma compared to normal plasma, directly linking a glycan change to a disease phenotype. However, the abstract lacks quantitative performance metrics (e.g., fold‑change, p‑value, AUC) and sample size, so the full text is needed to assess biomarker validity.

entities.evidence_sentence: Among these glycans, the abundance ratio of two representative glycoforms (fucosyl vs non-fucosyl) was significantly increased in HCC plasma relative to normal plasma.

title: Glycation of the complement regulatory protein CD59 is a novel biomarker for glucose handling in humans.

screening.reason: The study identifies soluble glycated CD59 (GCD59) as a glycan-based biomarker linked to glucose handling and diabetes, with clear quantitative associations (β, P-values, sample sizes) presented in the abstract. Full text is not needed as the abstract provides the glycan feature, disease context, specimen source, direction of association, and statistical evidence.
